doc.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: Hamilton concert series: J.J. Johnson and Nat Adderley
summary: The best concert he heard, J.J. Johnson with Tommy Flanagan, Tootie Heath and Nat Adderley, in spring 1958.

blocks.x: Did Hamilton have a concert series while you were here that brought jazz musicians to campus?

Yes they did. And that was interesting. We had more bop musicians than Dixieland players at that time. In fact probably the best concert I ever heard was J.J. Johnson, Tommy Flanagan, Tootie Heath, who was about 15 years old, and the cornet player was Nat Adderley.

And I remember it was over in Commons, what we call Commons, and they got up on the stage and J.J. said, “My schedule’s been messed up and I can only play for an hour, I’m going to play for an hour straight.” And it was one of the best hours of jazz I ever heard, because that was a great supporting cast. And then he had found a whole bunch of old guys — and I should know their names but I don’t — who came up with him and he said, “They’re going to do the second half of the concert.” Well these were guys who didn’t get to play a lot I guess. They were wonderful musicians, and of course they had the best time. So that thing went on for about four hours and that was a great afternoon.
I’ll bet. And I love Nat Adderley.

Yeah. And he was, I mean these guys were very young. This would have been the spring of ’58. And it was just the height of that season. I can’t remember who the bass player was on that job but you know Tommy Flanagan was —
